result.detailed_feedback:
**Element Layout (18.5 points):**
The layout is exceptionally clean and utilizes a logical split-screen approach: conceptual text on the left and dynamic animations on the right. The use of color-coding in the text (e.g., matching the yellow and red text to the corresponding vectors) significantly reduces cognitive load. The titles are clearly positioned at the top, and the use of the coordinate grid provides a necessary mathematical anchor for the visual elements.

**Attractiveness (19.0 points):**
The video adopts a high-quality minimalist aesthetic reminiscent of '3Blue1Brown' style. The color palette is vibrant yet professional, set against a high-contrast black background which makes the vector movements pop. The animations of vectors scaling and the tip-to-tail 'drone' movement are smooth and visually engaging, effectively capturing the viewer's attention.

**Logic Flow (19.5 points):**
The pedagogical scaffolding is nearly perfect. It starts with the basic 'recipe' (linear combinations), expands that to 'territory' (span), introduces the concept of redundancy (dependence) versus uniqueness (independence), and culminates in the 'minimalist toolkit' (basis). Each section flows naturally into the next, building complexity only after the previous layer is established.

**Accuracy & Depth (19.0 points):**
The content is mathematically rigorous while remaining accessible. The definition of span as 'the set of all reachable points' is an excellent pedagogical metaphor. The video correctly identifies that linear independence in 3D requires a vector to be 'off the plane' created by the first two. The depth is perfect for an introductory undergraduate or advanced high school level.

**Visual Consistency (19.5 points):**
Visual consistency is a major strength. The font, vector thickness, and color-coding scheme are maintained throughout the entire duration. Transitions between 2D and 3D conceptualizations are handled smoothly without breaking the established design language. The UI elements (grid lines, labels) remain uniform, creating a cohesive learning experience.

**Overall Summary:**
This is an outstanding educational video that provides a masterclass in visualizing abstract linear algebra concepts. By utilizing the 'drone' metaphor and the 'reachable territory' visualization, it transforms dry algebraic definitions into intuitive spatial concepts. The technical execution is flawless, and the pedagogical structure is highly effective for the target knowledge points.

**Key Strengths:**
• Excellent color-coordinated text that links definitions directly to the visual animations.
• Intuitive metaphors like 'Redundant Helper' for dependence and 'Essential Team' for independence.
• High-quality 3D visualization to explain how independence expands span into higher dimensions.
• Clean, distraction-free aesthetic that focuses entirely on the core concepts.

**Areas for Improvement:**
• Briefly showing the mathematical notation for the 'Span' set {v1, v2, ...} alongside the text might help bridge the gap to textbook problems.
• A quick visual mention of the origin (0,0) as a point always included in the span would add a layer of mathematical completeness.

B
An arrow is the classic geometric interpretation of a vector, as it visually represents the vector's two key properties: magnitude (length) and direction.

C
A linear combination is a sum of scalar multiples of vectors. The expression av + bw, where a and b are scalars, is the general form for a linear combination of two vectors v and w.

C
The span of a set of vectors is, by definition, the set of all possible linear combinations of those vectors. For two non-parallel vectors in a 2D plane, their linear combinations can form any vector in that entire plane.

B
This is the definition of linear dependence. If one vector can be expressed as a linear combination of the other two, it means it lies in the same plane (or line) and does not add a new dimension, making the set of vectors dependent.

C
A basis for a vector space is a set of linearly independent vectors that span the entire space. This means they are the fundamental building blocks for all other vectors in that space.
